mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds Rate is held constant above 5.25% for two consecutive months, the S&P 500 forward 20-day return is expected to be negative due to persistent risk aversion from higher policy rates compressing equity discounting.
failure_condition: Over a 60-day window, the 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from a zero-move baseline (t-test p > 0.05), or FEDFUNDS drops below 5.25 for three consecutive months without a subsequent positive return signal.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) by more than 0.5% in a single month is associated with negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns due to immediate market anticipation of future rate hikes.
failure_condition: Across 10 such triggered events, the 20-day forward returns are on average positive or equal to the mean of non-triggered periods (p > 0.05 two-tailed).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in employment (PAYEMS) of at least 10,000 jobs month-over-month for two consecutive months predicts a positive S&P 500 60-day forward return as labor market strength supports equity risk appetite.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS month-over-month change >= +10,000 for two consecutive months
failure_condition: During the same 60-day horizon, the forward return is negative in all such labor strength episodes (median negative).

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) exceeds 112.0 for two consecutive months, the S&P 500 20-day forward return is expected to be positive as it signals a strengthening supply-side momentum that feeds through to demand.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO month-over-month change >= +0.5 for two consecutive months
failure_condition: Across 8 such episodes, the 20-day forward return is not statistically higher than the mean of non-triggered windows (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in retail sales (HOUST) by more than 5% in a month coincides with a negative S&P 500 20-day forward return as it signals weakening consumer demand and potential equity valuation compression.
failure_condition: In 5 such events, the 20-day forward return is not statistically lower than the baseline (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of declining unemployment claims (UNRATE) below 4.0% are associated with a positive S&P 500 60-day forward return as it reflects labor market tightening and rising wage growth expectations.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE month-over-month change <= -0.2 for two consecutive months
failure_condition: Across 7 such episodes, the 60-day forward return is not statistically higher than the mean of non-triggered windows (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When both industrial production (INDPRO) and retail sales (HOUST) show simultaneous monthly gains of at least 2%, the S&P 500 20-day forward return is expected to be positive due to dual demand-side momentum.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO month-over-month change >= +2% AND HOUST month-over-month change >= +2%
failure_condition: In 10 such interaction events, the 20-day forward return is not statistically higher than the mean of single-variable triggers (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: During a regime of persistent monetary easing (FEDFUNDS < 4.00% for three consecutive months), the S&P 500 60-day forward return is predicted to be positive as lower policy rates reduce discounting of future cash flows.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS month-over-month change < -0.25 for three consecutive months
failure_condition: Across 6 such episodes, the 60-day forward return is not statistically higher than the average during periods of neutral policy (FEDFUNDS in [4.00%, 4.25%]).
